sources.title: Burnt out cars and shattered glass on Paris streets after protests turn to riots and looting

discussion.body: The numbers sit awkwardly together: a protest counted in hundreds of thousands, arrests in the thousands, and 1,500 damaged shops. The useful question is less whether the march was peaceful in essence than how quickly a crowd can be shadowed by people with a different plan.

That risks letting the looters set the story. The demonstrators' grievances — fuel prices, cost of living, schools — are the reason 550,000 people turned out; the damaged shops are a different story, and it is worth keeping the two from collapsing into one.

items.title: A Mostly Peaceful March, and 1,500 Damaged Shops
items.body: Some 550,000 demonstrators took to French streets on Saturday; police arrested about 1,800, and the protests were largely peaceful, according to the BBC's account. But widespread looting took place in Paris, Marseille and Lille, and more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters were injured, France's interior ministry said. The Retail and Trade Federation counted about 1,500 damaged shops and retailers. Demonstrators were protesting rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools.

sources.title: Noah Adams, longtime host of NPR's All Things Considered, has died

discussion.body: The train-and-small-town method is the real tribute: report where people are, not where the press conference is.
Listening is only half the craft; Block's 'always observing' points to the other half — the little notebook and the shorthand.

items.title: Noah Adams Listened for the Person, Not the Talking Point
items.body: Noah Adams, the writer, broadcaster and storyteller who hosted All Things Considered for 18 years, died Friday at his home in Yellow Springs, Ohio, at 84, according to his wife, Neenah Ellis. Adams would ride trains across the country or spend days in small towns talking to whoever he came across; he asked questions and listened. Melissa Block, who produced pieces alongside him before hosting the show herself, remembered him as 'always observing.' Ira Glass has repeatedly cited Adams's interviewing style as an inspiration for the feel and tone of This American Life.

sources.title: Sergei Loznitsa’s ‘Imperium’ Wins Best Film at BFI London Film Festival

discussion.body: A jury praising 'quiet resilience' in a 'noisy and often polemical world' is also announcing a documentary taste: patience over volume.
That framing risks making displacement palatable: 'quiet resilience' is the jury's phrase, and dignity is not the same as passivity.

items.title: A BFI Prize for the Documentary That Praises Quiet Resilience
items.body: At the 70th BFI London Film Festival, the Grierson Award for documentary went to Asmahan Bkerat's feature directorial debut, 'Concrete Land.' The film spends time with several generations of a mixed-race family in Jordan as they resist displacement and hostility. The jury, headed by 'Santosh' director Sandhya Suri, said it was 'refreshing, humbling and deeply relevant' to see the family's 'quiet resilience and dignity' in the face of 'the erasure of their culture and traditions,' in a noisy and often polemical world.

sources.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather

discussion.body: The most useful detail is the skeptic's: a shape in a lagoon can be a fallen tree. That's not cynicism; it's the baseline any search has to argue against.
But skepticism can become a ritual too. Previous attempts have come up short — which is a reason to demand evidence, not a reason to skip looking.

items.title: The Earhart Search Returns to a Shape in the Lagoon
items.body: A search for the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane has resumed at Nikumaroro Island, part of Kiribati, after severe weather caused researchers to stop for several days. The team is investigating the so-called Taraia Object, a feature spotted in the atoll's lagoon in aerial imagery. Some skeptics believe the object was just a tree that had fallen from the atoll into the lagoon.
